This toolkit is GraphQL-first for new Admin API automations while retaining legacy REST compatibility actions for older workflows and numeric-ID interoperability Copy page Authentication Details Composio-managed OAuth not available OAuth2 S2S_OAUTH2 Frequently Asked Questions How do I set up custom OAuth credentials for Shopify? Use your own app from the Shopify Dev Dashboard when you want to choose the scopes and the app name merchants see, or when the default app isn't available. Create the Shopify app Sign in to your Shopify admin. If you don't have a store, start one at shopify.com . Search for App Development in the admin search bar and open it, then click Build apps in Dev Dashboard . Click Create App , enter an app name, and click Create . Shopify opens the app's version configuration. Set App URL to your application's URL. Select the access scopes your tools need, such as read_products , write_products , read_orders , write_orders , read_customers , and read_inventory . Set the redirect URL to https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add . It must exactly match the auth config's oauth_redirect_uri field. Click Release , optionally add a version name and message, and click Release again. Open Settings in the left sidebar and copy the Client ID and Client Secret . Create the auth config in Composio In the Composio dashboard , go to Auth Configs → Create and select Shopify . Choose OAuth2 and your own credentials, then paste the Client ID and Client Secret. Keep the redirect URI as the value you registered in Shopify. Click Create Auth Config . Click Connect Account and enter the store subdomain: the permanent myshopify.com name, not a custom domain. For https://acme.myshopify.com , enter acme . You can find it under Settings → Domains in the Shopify admin. Install the app on the store and grant the permissions. Confirm the account shows Active on the auth config's Connected Accounts tab. See custom auth configs for the general flow. Scopes The default auth config requests read and write access to products, orders, customers, inventory, fulfillments, content, themes, discounts, draft orders, metaobjects, webhooks, and more. Select the same scopes on the Shopify app, and remove the ones you don't need from both. Why am I seeing "App not found" when connecting Shopify? The default Shopify OAuth app may be under review or expired. Use your own OAuth app or API authentication method until the default is restored. Shopify order update 403s can be caused by missing read_all_orders scope Check the scopes on the Shopify connection. If order reads or updates require access beyond the default order scope set, reconnect with the needed order scopes such as read_all_orders before retrying.
